title: Reading the fences a level closes with
target: How to read the fences, railings and barriers of a R.E.P.O. level so the theme and the route are clear before you commit to a room.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Enough light to see a railing

steps.do: Read the ceiling fence to place the theme.
steps.because: a ceiling fence is named for the ordinary level and a second one for the arctic theme (Fence - Ceiling, Fence - Ceiling Arctic)

steps.do: Test a catwalk railing before you lean on it.
steps.because: an arctic catwalk railing and a catwalk railing with its own sheets are named (Arctic Catwalk Railing, Catwalk Railing_DefaultMaterial_BaseColor3)

steps.do: Treat a stairs railing as part of the route.
steps.because: stairs railings are named by theme, a manor one and a catwalk one among them (Stair Manor Railing_DefaultMaterial_BaseColor, Stairs Catwalk Railing_DefaultMaterial_BaseColor)

steps.do: Do not read a misspelled name as a different piece.
steps.because: one arctic stairs railing is named with a second spelling of arctic (Arctiv Stairs Railing2)

steps.do: On the arena track, read the barrier shape before the corner.
steps.because: barriers are named for the places the track turns, splits, drops, crosses a stream and opens a gap (Arena Race Track Piece Barrier Turn, Arena Race Track Piece Barrier Split Path, Arena Race Track Piece Barrier Danger Gap)

steps.do: Take a plain fence as the level's own edge.
steps.because: the build names a plain fence of its own (Fence)

commonMistakes: Crossing a catwalk without checking what is above it.
Assuming two levels use the same fence for the same purpose.
Being surprised by a track that splits because the barrier was not read.
Treating the wizard stairs railing as a different piece of kit from the manor one.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
